segments.en: Yes. AI agents are the headline, but every guarantee (exhaustive match, no any, runtime-checked types, greppable code, stable diffs) helps people too.
segments.tr: 值得。AI 智能体是主打卖点，但每一项保证（穷尽的 match、没有 any、带运行时检查的类型、可以 grep 的代码、稳定的 diff）对人同样有帮助。

segments.en: 06 · For humans too
segments.tr: 06 · 对人同样有用

segments.en: Is Glyph worth it if I'm not using AI?
segments.tr: 如果我不用 AI，Glyph 还值得用吗？

segments.en: Yes. The AI-agent framing is the headline because agents break these things constantly, but every guarantee underneath is a plain engineering win a human gets directly. Fewer runtime surprises, smaller diffs, code you can actually grep. None of it requires an LLM.
segments.tr: 值得。以 AI 智能体为切入点，是因为智能体经常弄坏这些东西，但底下的每一项保证都是人能直接得到的工程收益：更少的运行时意外，更小的 diff，以及真正能 grep 的代码。这些都不需要大语言模型。

segments.en: These are language features, not AI features
segments.tr: 这些是语言特性，不是 AI 特性

segments.en: Strip the word "agent" out and read the list: no any, exhaustive match, errors as values, types that are checked at runtime, one declaration form per name, a canonical diff-stable format. Anyone who's written Rust, Elm, or OCaml recognizes these as the things that make a codebase pleasant to maintain. They were good ideas long before AI wrote code. Glyph just brings them to a TypeScript-shaped language you can adopt one file at a time.
segments.tr: 去掉“智能体”这个词，再看这份清单：没有 any，穷尽的 match，错误即值，在运行时检查的类型，每个名字只有一种声明形式，一种标准的、diff 稳定的格式。写过 Rust、Elm 或 OCaml 的人都会认出，这些正是让代码库易于维护的东西。早在 AI 写代码之前，它们就是好主意。Glyph 只是把它们带进一门形似 TypeScript、可以按文件逐个引入的语言。

segments.en: What you get, solo
segments.tr: 一个人用也能得到的好处

segments.en: Fewer 3am pages. Boundary data is validated by construction (User.parse), and a missing case is a compile error, not an undefined that surfaces in production.
segments.tr: 凌晨 3 点被叫醒的次数更少。边界数据在构造时就经过校验（User.parse），缺少的情况是编译错误，而不是在生产环境中冒出来的 undefined。

segments.en: Faster review. A one-line change is a one-line diff, so a reviewer reads the change, not the reformatting churn around it.
segments.tr: 审查更快。改一行就是一行 diff，所以审查者读的是改动本身，而不是周围的格式化噪音。

segments.en: You can find anything. grep "fn parseUser" lands on the definition: no overloads, barrels, or decorators scattering it.
segments.tr: 什么都能找到。grep "fn parseUser" 会落在定义上：没有重载、汇总导出文件或装饰器把它分散开。

segments.en: Easier onboarding. A small core with one way to do each thing means less tribal knowledge for the next person to learn.
segments.tr: 上手更容易。核心小，每件事只有一种做法，下一个人需要学习的隐性知识更少。

segments.en: So why lead with agents?
segments.tr: 那为什么以智能体为切入点？

segments.en: Because the payoff is bigger there. A human eventually learns to run the linter and handle the case; an agent reaches for any, forgets the arm, and merges it green, and it can't be trusted to keep the opt-in tooling on. The value of making the strictness non-optional compounds when a machine is writing the code. But the floor (the wins above) is there whether you use an agent or not.
segments.tr: 因为在那里回报更大。人最终会学会运行 linter、处理那个情况；而智能体会伸手去用 any，忘掉那个分支，然后在构建通过的状态下合并，你也不能指望它一直开着那些可选的工具。当代码由机器编写时，让严格性不可选的价值会成倍放大。但底线（上面那些好处）无论你是否使用智能体都在。

segments.en: Think of it as a stricter TypeScript that happens to be great for agents, not an agent tool you can only justify if you use one.
segments.tr: 可以把它看作一种更严格的 TypeScript，恰好非常适合智能体，而不是一个只有用智能体才说得过去的智能体工具。

segments.en: Where it stands
segments.tr: 当前状态

segments.en: The tradeoff
segments.tr: 取舍

segments.en: If you're starting something new, or your team already values ML-family discipline, the wins land immediately. If you're solo on a mature, well-tooled TS stack, it's a closer call: Glyph is an early preview, and that's a real cost to weigh.
segments.tr: 如果你在开始一个新项目，或者你的团队本来就重视 ML 家族语言的那种纪律，这些好处会立刻兑现。如果你一个人在一个成熟、工具齐全的 TS 技术栈上工作，就需要再掂量一下：Glyph 还是早期预览版，这是一项需要权衡的实际成本。

segments.en: Either way
segments.tr: 无论哪种情况

segments.en: The escape hatch is permanent: it compiles to readable TypeScript you own, so trying it on one module is cheap and reversible.
segments.tr: 逃生口是永久的：它编译成你自己掌握的可读 TypeScript，所以在一个模块上试用它成本很低，也可以随时撤回。
